paths.description: Homepage catalogue and global navigation; represents entry, consent, preferences, performance, privacy, and browsing.
British category listing; represents category/list template.
Representative video detail; represents the primary watch journey without initiating explicit media playback.
Search results for british; represents query/results and crawler rendering.
Signup dialog and email branch; represents account form, invalid state, autofill, and auth choices.

findings.summary: Infinite animations continue under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion evaluate probe found eight running 2,000 ms animations with infinite iteration while prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential animation in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference or disable it in a reduce query.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage across this multi-page navigation experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Page chrome does not respond to scroll position.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state or scroll-driven treatment while a large persistent header/sidebar occupies the browsing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress/shrinking-header treatment where it aids orientation.

findings.summary: Navigation provides little attention continuity.
findings.evidence: Representative route screenshots and CSS inspection show hard swaps with no directional transition, marker, or post-navigation highlight.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained directional View Transitions or target highlights to preserve orientation.

findings.summary: The consent prompt obscures the primary content on every fresh entry.
findings.evidence: Desktop, category, detail, signup, search, and 404 screenshots all open with a large centered consent overlay covering the page. Reject works, but content is interrupted before use.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface where legally permitted and preserve equal Accept/Reject choices without covering the primary task.

findings.summary: The consent modal is not exposed as a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows a modal, but the DOM probe found no dialog or role=dialog for it. The underlying page remains represented as ordinary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the consent UI with dialog/showModal(), an accessible name, focus containment, and a deliberate dismissal policy.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation, promotions, and sidebars crowd the content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport devotes substantial area to two nav rows, an age banner, a promotional banner, and a 200 px sidebar before the content grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent promotional chrome and collapse secondary navigation on constrained surfaces.

findings.summary: Mobile receives a 1024 px desktop layout.
findings.evidence: At viewport 360x800, layout measured scrollWidth and innerWidth of 1024 against a 360 px visual viewport, producing 664 px horizontal overflow on home, category, and detail paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the desktop minimum layout width, use intrinsic grid sizing, and validate all templates at narrow viewports.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero container rules; narrow captures retain desktop sidebar/card geometry rather than adapting to available component width.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and focused @container rules for reused result grids, cards, and navigation modules.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch targeting are inadequate.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline-style none on sampled links, buttons, and search input; Lighthouse also found target-size failures. Several visible controls are 25-32 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and size interactive targets to at least 44 CSS px or provide adequate spacing.

findings.summary: Lab LCP misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.1 s and FCP 2.3 s; the unthrottled trace measured LCP 1.40 s, so the risk is condition-sensitive rather than universal.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource and reduce render-blocking and startup work, then verify with field data.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache delivery leave measurable savings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported about 1,130 ms render-blocking savings and 113 KiB cache-lifetime savings; HAR confirms parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, and set useful immutable cache lifetimes for versioned assets.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 57 KiB unused CSS and 26 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR records 61 scripts and about 998 KiB transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route-specific bundles, conditionally load modal/account code, and remove unused selectors and legacy output.

findings.summary: Controls and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 0.72 with button-name and link-name failures; the custom probe found 43 blank links and an unlabeled category-filter input.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable element a programmatic name, label the filter, and hide decorative links/icons from the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 13 color-contrast failures and links that rely on color alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/surface tokens to WCAG AA and add a non-color cue for links.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and structure are not reliable.
findings.evidence: The focus walk reported outline none across sampled controls and links; Lighthouse also reported malformed list structure and an ill-formed agent accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible :focus-visible styles, correct list semantics, and verify logical tab order with the consent modal open and closed.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and the layout does not reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no in the viewport meta and target-size failures; 360 px layout evidence shows 664 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no, retain maximum-scale at least 5, enlarge targets, and make templates reflow without two-dimensional scrolling.

findings.summary: Many images lack intrinsic dimensions or are oversized.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 29 of 36 images without width/height and 14 oversized images; Lighthouse also flagged unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and tighten srcset/sizes to rendered card widths.

findings.summary: No sitemap is exposed at the conventional URL or declared in robots.txt.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is crawlable but contains no Sitemap directive, and /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap indexes for public templates and declare them in robots.txt; keep canonical host policy consistent.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks entity and share-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter Card tags on a public media catalogue homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata; add VideoObject metadata on detail pages.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show a CSP limited to frame-ancestors, missing nosniff, and no response Referrer-Policy. Cookie evidence found four non-Secure cookies and three SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, strict Referrer-Policy, longer HSTS, and Secure/Lax cookie defaults unless cross-site use is required.

findings.summary: The initial page has a broad third-party and identifier-bearing footprint.
findings.evidence: Before consent, network evidence saw 11 third-party origins. Rendered external URLs include statsUID/session-style parameters and the document declares referrer=unsafe-url.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent third-party calls, remove identifiers from outbound URLs, and use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: Signup offers passwords and federated identity but no phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The signup path exposes Google, X, email, and a new-password field; no WebAuthn/passkey capability was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration/authentication alongside recovery-safe existing methods.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are only partial.
findings.evidence: HSTS is only one day; CSP contains only frame-ancestors; nosniff and response Referrer-Policy are absent, while Permissions-Policy only controls client hints.
findings.suggestedFix: Harden HSTS, CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types and origin isolation for the script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: The localized surface is not robust to bidirectional layout.
findings.evidence: html lang=en is present, but dir is omitted and the CSS probe counted 608 physical left/right rules with no container-query modernization.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang and dir per locale and migrate layout-critical physical properties to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: Email signup fields are unlabeled and invalid submission gives no clear error.
findings.evidence: After opening email signup, two email inputs had no labels, autocomplete=off, and required=false; attempting submit produced no role=alert or aria-invalid feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real labels, required constraints, :user-invalid, inline actionable messages, and an aria-live error summary after attempted submission.

findings.summary: Signup blocks useful autofill.
findings.evidence: Email signup sets autocomplete=off on email fields; the password field correctly uses new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email and the appropriate username/name tokens while preserving new-password.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and risks instability.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 14 oversized images, 14 legacy-format images, 29 missing dimensions, and 8 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve tighter responsive candidates in AVIF/WebP, add dimensions, and lazy-load non-critical images.

findings.summary: Startup performs disproportionate script and third-party work.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 142 requests and 1.79 MB transferred, including 61 scripts and 11 third-party origins; Lighthouse found unused code.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level request/byte budget and defer optional ads, identity, creator, and modal bundles until needed.

findings.summary: Third-party media and promotion load before demonstrated user intent.
findings.evidence: The initial capture contacts 11 third-party origins, including advertising/media hosts, while the first viewport is still behind consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional ad/media requests on consent and visibility, cache stable assets, and avoid speculative promotional media.

findings.summary: Search and account capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic browsing scored 0.5 with a malformed accessibility tree, and no WebMCP registrations were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Once stable for target browsers, expose safe search/navigation tools with WebMCP and first repair the accessibility tree.

taskList.title: Rebuild all templates for true mobile reflow and zoom
Repair accessible names, contrast, focus, and dialog semantics
Harden CSP, cookies, referrer policy, and pre-consent data flows
Reduce startup code, render blocking, and third-party work
Fix image dimensions, responsive candidates, and loading policy
Make signup humane and autofill-friendly; add passkeys
Honor reduced motion and add restrained navigation continuity
Reduce intrusive chrome and implement semantic consent
Use logical properties across localized layouts
